findings.title: Overwrite safety contract only defined for the two top-level files; `.github/instructions/` and `.github/prompts/` are unprotected
findings.description: The sequence step 4 checks the managed marker in `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and `AGENTS.md` only, and "Files Changed" adds `isManagedCopilotFiles(projectPath)` for just those two files. Yet the design decision at line 65 says "Both Claude and Copilot generated files carry `[//]: # (context-forge:managed)`" — i.e., every emitted `.instructions.md` and `.prompt.md` gets a marker that nothing in the CLI checks before overwrite. These two directories are exactly where users author their own content: `.github/prompts/` is the documented VS Code location for user prompt files (see the referenced tool guide's examples), and skill names like `commit` / `review-pr` are plausible collision points. A user-authored, unmarked `commit.prompt.md` would be silently replaced by the guide script with no prompt and no `.bak`, violating the plan's safety contract ("first-run warns before overwriting unmanaged user content"). The design should specify per-file marker checks and backup/collision behavior for the instructions/prompts directories, and state explicitly whether backup-to-`.bak` runs even when `--yes` is passed (the 202 contract for `CLAUDE.md` is "backup runs regardless of `--yes`"; this slice's "prompt (or skip with `--yes`), backup to `.bak`" is ambiguous on that point).

findings.title: Two plan success criteria have no verification counterpart in the slice design
findings.description: The slice plan's success criteria include: (1) "Path→applyTo translation correctly converts Claude frontmatter to Copilot frontmatter for split rule files," and (2) "Manual verification: an AI agent in VS Code Copilot can read `.github/copilot-instructions.md` + `AGENTS.md` and follow project conventions as well as Claude does with `CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/rules/`." The Test Coverage section assigns a test to every other criterion (generation, managed re-run, unmanaged prompt, worktree propagation, target validation, init end-to-end) but has no item for the translation or for the in-Copilot behavior check. This matters disproportionately because the plan rates the slice Risk: Med and names "frontmatter translation correctness" explicitly, and because the translation lives in a bash script in the guides submodule — the one component the CLI-side test list cannot reach. The design should name where translation correctness is verified (fixture-based tests in the submodule script, or a CLI-side smoke test asserting emitted `applyTo` values for a known rule set) and add the manual Copilot-verification item.

findings.title: Tool-guide reference/promotion criterion dropped from the design
findings.description: The plan lists as a success criterion: "Tool guide (`project-documents/user/tool-guides/copilot-vscode/setup-ide.md`) referenced in slice design, promoted to a proper published tool guide if needed." The slice design never references that file — its VS Code format facts (`applyTo` comma-separated globs, prompt-file frontmatter fields `name`/`description`/`argument-hint`/`agent`/`model`/`tools`, "multiple instruction files combine with no guaranteed order", `AGENTS.md` folder-locality) all come from that guide, so the traceability the plan asks for is missing. Additionally, the file as it exists is a raw chat export (embedded CDN logo ``, footnote spans, a closing "Would you like..." question), not a published guide; the "promoted … if needed" half of the criterion is silently skipped. Either add a reference (and the format facts it anchors), or record a deliberate deferral with a named follow-up.

findings.title: Onboarding-time NFR from the parent architecture is not restated
findings.description: The 200 architecture's design goal is "from `npm install` to useful context output in under two minutes," and this slice adds a branch to that path (`cf init --ide copilot` routes through `setupIdeAction` plus the new copilot safety checks and worktree propagation). The slice doc does not restate the target. The new work is a single script invocation and file copies, so risk to the two-minute budget is low — but if the copilot compilation in the guides script is expected to take materially longer than the claude compile, that should be noted against the target.

findings.title: Partial-run failure of the guide script and propagation copy errors not explicitly handled
findings.description: Step 5's `execFileSync` inherits the claude path's failure behavior (non-zero exit → clear error, verified in `setup-ide.ts`), and the Risks section covers the out-of-sync-submodule case well. Two modes are not addressed: (a) the script failing mid-write (e.g., `copilot-instructions.md` written with marker, `AGENTS.md` not yet) — re-run appears safe by construction since managed files skip the prompt, but that should be stated; (b) `propagateToWorktrees` copy failures against a registered worktree whose path is stale or unwritable — the current claude block lets `fs.copyFileSync` throw to `handleError`, and the parallel copilot block would do the same, which is acceptable, but worth a sentence so implementers don't "improve" it inconsistently. Neither blocks the design; both are one-liners.
